description: ABSTRACT-CLAIM EXPANSION: a we/this study/the present study subject, up to three intervening words, and replicate/replicated/replicates, followed within the same clause and at most 120 characters by an author-year-shaped reference. Two bibliographic syntax families: (1) a capitalised ASCII/Latin-1 name at a whitespace or opening-parenthesis/bracket boundary, optionally followed by et al., and colleagues or a study noun, an optional comma and optional parenthesis, then a 19xx/20xx year; (2) a year followed by 'by' and a capitalised name, or capitalised author names joined by and/&/et al. and an explicit study/paper/work/findings/results/analysis/experiment noun. The name itself is case-sensitive despite the engine's (?i) prefix; year boundaries prevent matching a prefix of a larger number. Citation separators are horizontal whitespace, commas or parentheses; the citation cannot cross a newline, and a year-first by-author name must end at a delimiter or end of text. Bare dates and arbitrary word-plus-number text do not admit a record. These are general citation shapes, not a semantic proof that a proper noun is an author, that a target is named, or that the study completed. No specific surname, paper or work-id exceptions. Precedence 737 remains below extension (738), title/curated admissions (740-760) and structural discards (935-960), and above failure-prior (736), general (735) and the fallible type crosswalk (500). Repository DOI and replication-package/materials/data/code title exclusions remain copied from general. Requires an abstract, assigns no vocabulary, only schedules the two-voter screen. Original evidence is historical: the revised pattern removes the noisy measured arm and its precision is not established by that arm's 59.8% estimate. See analysis/admission_rules_2026_10/README.md and citation_review_patterns.json.
